question: How do I measure sales efficiency at different ARR scales?
answer:
Efficiency scales inversely with ARR growth. Early stage ($1–5M): target **CAC payback 12–18 months**. Mid-market ($5–50M): **9–12 months**. Enterprise ($50M+): **6–9 months**. Calculate: Sales & marketing spend ÷ (New ARR this quarter × gross margin). **The mechanics change by stage:** 1. **Below $5M ARR** — outbound + founder selling dominates. Track per-rep quota attainment, not blended efficiency. ACV too volatile. 2. **$5–20M** — outbound + inbound mix. CAC payback + **magic number** (net new ARR ÷ prior-quarter S&M spend, target ≥0.75) reveals if you're growing efficiently or burning. 3. **$20–50M** — land + expand motion. Split **land CAC** (new customers) from **expansion uplift**. Expansion has 2–3 month shorter payback; don't let it mask a broken land motion. 4. **$50M+** — net new becomes a rounding error. **Expansion CAC** (cost-to-expand) and **Win Rate × ASP** matter more than blended metrics. **Benchmark drill:** | Stage | CAC Payback | Magic # | Win Rate | |-------|------------|---------|----------| | <$5M | 18–24m | N/A | 15–20% | | $5–20M | 12–18m | 0.5–0.75 | 20–25% | | $20–50M | 9–12m | 0.75–1.0 | 25–30% | | $50M+ | 6–9m | N/A | 30%+ | **Action:** At each stage, you're measuring a different engine.
